speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Could you tell me your age and when we first noticed your high blood pressure? Also, are you experiencing any headaches, vision changes, or shortness of breath?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the blood pressure differ significantly between his arms and legs, or has anyone noticed a weak pulse in his legs? I'd like to listen to his chest for a heart murmur while feeling the pulses in his extremities.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the blood pressure is elevated only in the right arm, I need to ask if anyone has noticed a weak or delayed pulse in his legs compared to his arms. I will also listen carefully for a specific type of heart murmur, often heard on the back, which could indicate a narrowing of the aorta.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Born full term with an uneventful neonatal period. Social history: Patient attends kindergarten. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco smoke.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the isolated hypertension in the right arm, I need to check if his leg pulses are weak or delayed compared to his arm pulses. I will also listen carefully to his chest and back for a systolic murmur that might suggest coarctation of the aorta.

speaker: Patient
text: All systems review is essentially negative as reported by the mother.

speaker: Doctor
text: I will now physically examine you to compare the strength and timing of your arm and leg pulses, and listen to your chest and back for any murmurs. REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram. REQUEST IMAGES: Cardiac MRI.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Blood Pressure Right Upper Extremity 150/80 mm Hg; Heart Rate and Respiratory Rate normal for age. Cardiovascular Examination: 2+ radial pulses, trace femoral pulses; Normal S1/S2 with a 2/6 long systolic murmur and systolic ejection click over the left sternal border and back; Normal point of maximal impact. Diagnostic Tests: Echocardiogram shows narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, consistent with coarctation, and normal left ventricular function. Blood Pressure Differential: 150/80 mm Hg in upper extremities compared to lower values in lower extremities. Chest X-ray: Normal heart size, no rib notching observed. Note: Cardiac MRI was requested but results are not available in the current dataset.

speaker: Doctor
text: The examination and echocardiogram confirm a narrowing of the aorta with significantly weaker pulses in your legs, which points directly to coarctation of the aorta. Since the diagnosis is clear, I will proceed with the final assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta.
